## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 21 (titled *Nagga*, "Bathing naked") is a disciplinary training rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning Buddhist nuns [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who bathes naked commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Conze 1954; Hüsken 1997]. In her analysis of the nuns' legal corpus, Ute Hüsken contrasts this explicit prohibition against naked bathing in Pācittiya 21 with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 2, which specifically proscribes the removal of pubic hair [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records a passage-level parallel to this text in the *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8) of the Khandhaka, as well as corresponding rules in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 21), the *Parivāra* (Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 21), and the vinaya traditions of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-tradition connections through automatic alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus identifies 203 shared textual segments across 56 texts, consisting of formulaic legal formulations shared most extensively with the *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18), other nuns' rules (notably Bi-Vb Pc40, Pc24, Pc25, and Pc15), monk vinaya rules (such as Bu-Vb Pc58 and Pd4), and the *Katāpattivāra* sections of the *Parivāra* (Pvr 1.2 and Pvr 2.2) [DharmaNexus].
